Production ML systems degrade due to data drift, concept drift, delayed labels, or feedback loops. A robust monitoring and debugging plan is essential to detect and resolve issues quickly.
Monitoring Plan
1. Feature Drift Detection
Track statistical changes in input features over time.
Use Population Stability Index (PSI), KL divergence, or Kolmogorov-Smirnov test. Example: If user age distribution shifts from mostly 25-35 to 35-45, the model may underperform for the new demographic. Tools: Evidently AI, WhyLabs, Fiddler.
2. Label Delay Monitoring
Track time between prediction and ground-truth label availability.
Set up alerts if label delay exceeds a threshold. Example: In ad click prediction, if labels take 7 days instead of 1 day, model retraining may be delayed. Mitigation: Use proxy metrics (e.g., click-through rate) until true labels arrive.
3. Feedback Loop Monitoring
Detect if model predictions influence future inputs.
Example: A recommendation model suggests items → users click more on those items → model sees more positive labels for those items → reinforces bias. Mitigation: Use exploration (epsilon-greedy, bandits)

We need to explain why a PyTorch DistributedDataParallel (DDP) job can hang when some ranks skip a conditional branch. Provide a minimal debugging checklist and two correct ways to restructure the model.

Let's break down the problem:

- DDP wraps a model and synchronizes gradients across ranks during backward pass. It expects all ranks to execute the same operations in the same order, because it uses collective communication (all-reduce) on gradients. If some ranks skip a conditional branch that contains parameters or operations that produce gradients, then the DDP's expected sequence of gradient reductions is broken. Specifically, DDP uses "bucket" based gradient reduction: it expects each rank to compute gradients for the same set of parameters in the same order. If some ranks skip a branch that contains parameters, those ranks won't have gradients for those parameters, so the all-reduce for those buckets will never be triggered, or the ranks will wait indefinitely for the missing gradients. This leads to a hang.

- The hang occurs because DDP's reducer expects all ranks to participate in the all-reduce for each bucket. If a rank doesn't compute gradients for a bucket (because it skipped the branch), it won't call the all-reduce, and other ranks will wait forever
